A <TEXTITOPEN_0001>big ph site<TEXTITCLOSE_0001> is any site <MATH_0001> as in
Sites, Definition <REF_0001> constructed as follows:
<STRUCT_0001>
<STRUCT_0002> Choose any set of schemes <MATH_0002>, and any set of ph coverings
<MATH_0003> among these schemes.
<STRUCT_0003> As underlying category take any category <MATH_0004>
constructed as in Sets, Lemma <REF_0002>
starting with the set <MATH_0005>.
<STRUCT_0004> Choose any set of coverings as in
Sets, Lemma <REF_0003> starting with the
category <MATH_0006> and the class of ph coverings,
and the set <MATH_0007> chosen above.
<STRUCT_0005>

<STRUCT_0001>
See the remarks following Definition <REF_0001>
for motivation and explanation regarding the definition of big sites.

<STRUCT_0002><STRUCT_0003>
Before we continue with the introduction of the big ph site of
a scheme <MATH_0001>, let us point out that the topology on a big ph site
<MATH_0002> is in some sense induced from the ph topology
on the category of all schemes.

Let <MATH_0001> be a big ph site as in
Definition <REF_0001>.
Let <MATH_0002>.
Let <MATH_0003> be an arbitrary ph covering of <MATH_0004>.
<STRUCT_0001>
<STRUCT_0002> There exists a covering <MATH_0005> of <MATH_0006> in the site
<MATH_0007> which refines <MATH_0008>.
<STRUCT_0003> If <MATH_0009> is a standard ph covering, then
it is tautologically equivalent to a covering of <MATH_0010>.
<STRUCT_0004> If <MATH_0011> is a Zariski covering, then
it is tautologically equivalent to a covering of <MATH_0012>.
<STRUCT_0005>

For each <MATH_0001> choose an affine open covering <MATH_0002>
such that each <MATH_0003> maps into an affine open subscheme of <MATH_0004>. By
Lemmas <REF_0001> and <REF_0002>
the refinement <MATH_0005> is a ph covering
of <MATH_0006> as well. Hence we may assume each <MATH_0007> is affine, and maps into
an affine open <MATH_0008> of <MATH_0009>. Applying
Sets, Lemma <REF_0003>
we see that <MATH_0010> is isomorphic to an object of <MATH_0011>.
But then <MATH_0012> as a finite type scheme over <MATH_0013>
is isomorphic to an object <MATH_0014> of <MATH_0015> by a second
application of
Sets, Lemma <REF_0004>.
The covering <MATH_0016> refines <MATH_0017>
(because they are isomorphic).
Moreover, <MATH_0018> is combinatorially equivalent to a
covering <MATH_0019> of <MATH_0020> in the site
<MATH_0021> by
Sets, Lemma <REF_0005>.
The covering <MATH_0022> is a refinement as in (1).
In the situation of (2), (3) each of the
schemes <MATH_0023> is isomorphic to an object of <MATH_0024> by
Sets, Lemma <REF_0006>,
and another application of
Sets, Lemma <REF_0007>
gives what we want.
